newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber extends falls at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber extends falls at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower on Monday as buyers continued to ignore a market craving for consumer demand, traders said.
"There's absolutely no activity to report today," said a trader. "The market was quiet and cold."
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted July RSS1 buyer at 259.50 cents ($1.04) a kg, down four cents from Friday. July SMR20 buyer fell half cent to 245.
Trading houses offered the SMR20 at 243 cents, SMR CV at 312, SMR L at 292 and latex at 213.
The government announced on Monday that it will hold rubber processors responsible for paying a replanting and research cess from next year and also retrench 1,246 civil servants from the industry.
But traders said the news had no effect on the market.
Traders said prices were expected to stay soft and fall between one and two cents daily through the week.
The INRO five-day average was 200.15 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on June 27 from 201.58 on June 26. The daily indicator was at 196.92 against 197.95 previously.
